rationale: Crosslake remains an active Tiger-backed communications-infrastructure platform. Regulatory evidence supports the Tiger Fund II Crosslake AIV chain and a 93.26% indirect interest at the 2018 disclosure date, but not current sole ownership or a current percentage. Current company disclosure supports more than 25 backbone PoPs plus separately identified extranet sites, rather than more than 40 owned PoPs. No later Tiger exit, sale or signed pending sponsor transaction was found.
recommendedChanges: Retain one active Crosslake Fibre record at crosslake-fibre|canada-united-states with Tiger Infrastructure Partners as the active manager.
Preserve the December 7, 2017 public entry date and attribute the investment to Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund II through the two Crosslake AIVs and Connect Investments LP.
Record 93.26% as a historical indirect interest at the 2018 regulatory disclosure date; set the current stake to NOT_PUBLICLY_DISCLOSED and do not present Tiger as a proven sole owner.
Correct the operating scale to two named live systems totaling 681 kilometres and more than 25 backbone PoPs, while labeling additional sites as extranet reach rather than owned PoPs.
Keep the Lake Ontario and CrossChannel systems, Maple Leaf route joint venture, PoPs and other route projects beneath the canonical Crosslake platform.
unresolvedQuestions: Crosslake's current ultimate parent, Tiger percentage, minority-holder composition and any post-2018 dilution are not publicly disclosed.
Any nonpublic debt financing, refinancing or recapitalization is not publicly disclosed.
The ownership, IRU and lease split for route extensions and extranet reach is not publicly disclosed.
Wall-New Jersey-to-Long Island and Maple Leaf completion status require later current-operating verification before inclusion in active scale.
